title: Retail Installment Contracts: Funds Cushion Days on Payoff Statements
content:
**Rule.** A payoff statement on a contract under Retail Installment Contracts adds funds cushion days according to the fee-bearing returns on the contract in the rolling 12 months ending on the quote date, read against the tier's returned-payment restriction count:

- when those returns reach the tier's restriction count, **1** day is added;
- when there is at least one but fewer than the count, **3** days are added;
- with none, no cushion is added.

| Tier | Restriction count | Fee-bearing returns giving 1 day | giving 3 days | giving none |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tier 6 Fresh Start | 2 | 2 or more | 1 | 0 |
| Tier 5 Rebuild | 2 | 2 or more | 1 | 0 |
| Tier 4 Standard | 2 | 2 or more | 1 | 0 |
| Tier 3 Advantage | 3 | 3 or more | 1 or 2 | 0 |
| Tier 2 Preferred | 3 | 3 or more | 1 or 2 | 0 |
| Tier 1 Select | 3 | 3 or more | 1 or 2 | 0 |

Fee-bearing returns are returns for insufficient funds, account closed, stop payment or uncollected funds; the rolling 12 months run from records dated later than the same calendar day 12 months before the quote date (the last day of that month when that day does not exist) through the quote date.

**Hypothetical case.** A Tier 3 Advantage contract with two insufficient-funds returns and one bank-error return in the window: two fee-bearing returns, fewer than 3, so 3 days are added. A Tier 5 Rebuild contract with the same history reaches its count of 2, so 1 day is added.
